bel_linen_seller.text: Linen, madam, sir, or anybody else. Touch the tablecloth. Go on, it is cooler than you think.
Linen comes from flax, the blue-flowered plant. Belfast made so much of it that it was nicknamed Linenopolis.
In the 1690s a Huguenot called Louis Crommelin set up near Lisburn and improved the trade. His name is still on a few things.

then.text: Mind you tell Nuala the girls' names are in the back of the order books. She'll find them if she looks.
I went in at fourteen, the same as my mother. Before that the half-timers did mornings in the mill and afternoons at school, or the other way round.
The sheds were so loud you learned to talk without a sound. Everybody could lip-read by Friday. You'd a whole conversation going across forty looms and the foreman never heard a word.
The doffers were the wee ones. They swapped the full bobbins for empty ones, fast, under the frames. The mills ran on small hands and big wages for somebody else.
Tell Nuala to write the doffers down. And then go to the Wall. That's a different kind of hands, but they were hands.

else.text: Have a look at the bolt on the table first, love. The cloth will tell you what I'd only waffle about.
